title: Retries, timeouts and jitter
summary: A retry spends more of the server's capacity to raise your odds of success. Done once, with backoff, jitter, a cap and a deadline, it absorbs blips. Done at every layer, it turns a blip into an outage.
useIf: Calls fail transiently with 429, 408 or 5xx, and you must decide what to retry, how long to wait and when to stop.
avoidIf: The error is a quota or billing failure, a client error, or a side-effecting call with no idempotency key.

explain.md: OpenAI's guidance is to treat `Retry-After` as a minimum plus a small random delay, otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter, cap attempts and total time, never retry quota or billing errors, and count SDK retries so loops do not multiply [[r16]]. AWS explains why: capped backoff alone leaves clients retrying in clusters, and **jitter** spreads them out and cuts total calls [[r18]]. Its **full jitter** variant sleeps a random time between 0 and the capped exponential value.

**Layers multiply.** With three retries at each of five stacked layers, a failing database sees 3^5 = 243 times the load, which makes recovery unlikely. Retry at one point in the stack, and limit retries locally with a token bucket [[tr3]]. **Timeouts** come from the downstream latency percentile: choose an acceptable false-timeout rate such as 0.1% and read the p99.9 latency, padded when the percentile is close to the median [[tr3]]. For LLM calls use separate limits for time to first token and for total generation, since output length drives total time. Only **idempotent** calls are safe to retry; a tool that charges a card needs an idempotency key first [[tr3]].

pitfalls.symptom: A small provider blip becomes a long outage
pitfalls.cause: SDK, framework and app each retry three times, multiplying traffic
pitfalls.fix: Keep one retry layer, set the others to zero and cap total attempts and time

pitfalls.symptom: Thousands of clients return at the same second
pitfalls.cause: Backoff without jitter keeps clients synchronised
pitfalls.fix: Add full jitter and honour `Retry-After` as a minimum

pitfalls.cause: A tool call was retried after a timeout and was not idempotent
pitfalls.fix: Send an idempotency key and check state before repeating side effects

pitfalls.symptom: Retries keep failing with the same 429
pitfalls.cause: The error was exhausted quota or billing
pitfalls.fix: Detect it, stop retrying, alert and degrade

scenarios.title: Three layers, three retries each
scenarios.situation: A service calls a framework that calls an SDK that calls a model. Each layer makes up to three attempts with no jitter. During a provider slowdown the load on the model endpoint multiplies and recovery drags on.
unknowns: Which layer should own the policy?
scenarios.question: What do you change?

options.name: One retry layer with jitter, `Retry-After` honoured, capped attempts and a total deadline; other layers set to zero
options.why: Three attempts at each of three layers is up to 27 attempts per request at the bottom. One owned policy removes the multiplication.
options.tradeoff: One team owns retry behaviour and must expose it as configuration.

options.name: Raise the base delay in every layer
options.tradeoff: Layers still multiply and latency grows.

options.name: Add more retries to be safe
options.why: More attempts add load when the dependency is overloaded.
options.tradeoff: More retries are right only for rare transient faults.

flips.if: The deadline is under a second
flips.then: No retries; use a fallback or fail fast.
Add a circuit breaker and shed load.

scenarios.takeaway: Retry at one layer. Layers multiply.

scenarios.title: The stream breaks halfway
scenarios.situation: A chat UI streams tokens. After 300 tokens the connection drops with a 5xx.
constraints: The user has seen partial text
Generation is not idempotent in content
A deterministic resume is not available
unknowns: Can the client resume from a partial state?
scenarios.question: What should the client do?

options.name: Keep the partial text visible, mark it incomplete and let the user retry or continue
options.why: A silent restart replaces text the user has read and doubles cost.

options.name: Retry the whole call and replace the text
options.why: Often fine when little text was shown.
options.tradeoff: The new answer can differ and the first tokens are paid twice.

options.name: Retry in a loop until the stream completes
options.why: Repeated partial runs waste tokens and risk a retry storm.
options.tradeoff: Right only with a hard cap and when no text has been shown yet.

flips.if: Background mode stores the response server-side
flips.then: Poll or resume it rather than regenerating.

scenarios.takeaway: After the user has seen output, retrying changes their experience.

scenarios.title: An agent that issues refunds
scenarios.situation: An agent calls a refund tool that times out at the client. The refund may or may not have been processed.
constraints: Idempotency keys are supported by the payment API
unknowns: Does the API return the prior result for a repeated key?
scenarios.question: How do you retry?

options.name: Retry with the same idempotency key, or look up status before repeating
options.why: The key makes repeated attempts safe, so the side effect happens once.
options.tradeoff: Requires key generation, storage and a status endpoint.

options.name: Do not retry and escalate to a human
Retry blindly with backoff
options.tradeoff: Blind retries are right only for read-only calls.

flips.if: The API offers no idempotency or status

scenarios.takeaway: Side effects need idempotency before retries.

quiz.q: Five stacked layers each retry up to 3 times when the bottom service fails. How many times the original load can the bottom service see?
quiz.explain: Retries multiply: 3^5 = 243. AWS uses this example to argue for retrying at a single point in the stack [[tr3]].

quiz.q: What is the main flaw in this retry policy?

code.code:
for attempt in range(10):
    r = send()
    if r.ok: return r
    time.sleep(2 ** attempt)

options: No jitter, no cap, no deadline, and it retries every error
quiz.explain: Without jitter clients stay synchronised, the delay is uncapped (2^9 is 512 seconds), there is no total deadline and quota or 4xx errors are retried too. Exponential backoff itself is fine [[r18]].

quiz.q: Which failures are reasonable to retry with backoff and a cap?
options: 429 from a rate window with Retry-After
quiz.explain: Transient rate and overload errors can succeed later. Quota or billing exhaustion and 400s fail again [[r16]].

flashcards.back: Sleep a random time between 0 and min(cap, base x 2^attempt). It spreads retries and cuts total calls versus no jitter.

flashcards.front: Why retry at only one layer?
flashcards.back: Retries multiply across layers. Three retries at five layers is 3^5 = 243 times the load on the bottom service.
As a minimum wait, plus a small random delay. Never retry quota or billing errors.
